title: Man killed in stabbing inside South Station during rush hour, officials say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was fatally stabbed inside South Station during rush hour on Wednesday evening in Boston.
The victim, unidentified by officials, was involved in an altercation on an escalator before being stabbed.
The suspect, described only as male, remains at large; police are reviewing video evidence and interviewing witnesses.

title: Body found at TD Garden, police say
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Boston police received a report of an unconscious person near TD Garden on Wednesday evening at 5:15 p.m.
The person was found deceased inside the parking garage adjacent to TD Garden, according to preliminary information.
The incident is under investigation, with Boston police handling inquiries instead of TD Garden representatives.

title: Athol man charged with child pornography possession
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Kristopher Ambrozewicz, 35, from Athol, was charged with possession of child pornography by federal prosecutors.
A search of Ambrozewicz's home revealed videos of child sexual abuse material on his cell phone, authorities stated.
Ambrozewicz is scheduled for arraignment in Worcester Federal Court, facing up to 20 years in prison if convicted.

title: Police: Person held pregnant woman hostage with gun during dramatic chase on I-93 in Milton
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A pregnant woman was held hostage in an SUV during a police chase on I-93 in Milton.
Suspect Dominic Hampton-Boyd crashed into eight vehicles and attempted to flee before being arrested.
Hampton-Boyd is charged with multiple offenses; the extent of the woman's injuries is undisclosed.

title: Stoughton town manager contradicts police chief who accused him of tampering with Sandra Birchmore investigation
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Stoughton Town Manager Thomas Calter denies allegations of tampering with the Sandra Birchmore investigation.
Police Chief Donna McNamara's lawsuit claims Calter pressured her to resign and made discriminatory comments.
Calter and McNamara are both on paid administrative leave amid ongoing legal and departmental conflicts.

title: Nearly 30 people arrested after investigation into drug trafficking in Western Mass.
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: 28 people were arrested in a drug trafficking investigation in Chicopee, Holyoke, and Springfield.
Law enforcement seized over 12 firearms, cocaine, fentanyl pills, and heroin during "Operation Pinky Promise".
The operation was led by the FBI’s Western Massachusetts Gang Task Force and Chicopee Police Department.

title: Patriots stock watch 2.0: Who’s rising and falling ahead of preseason opener?
author: Khari A. Thompson
bullets: Romeo Doubs and Drake Maye stood out in Patriots practices, showing strong performances ahead of preseason.
Elijah Ponder and Eli Raridon made significant plays, with Raridon receiving more first-team reps as a tight end.
Behren Morton and Jam Miller's stock declined due to limited playing time and competition from teammates.

title: Public art tiles stolen out of sidewalk in Dedham, town says
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Four art tiles from the Sawmill Park Pollinator Pathway in Dedham were reported stolen by town officials.
The tiles were part of a project created with a Massachusetts Community Biodiversity Grant and feature local artists' designs.
Despite the theft, the park's ribbon-cutting ceremony will proceed on August 19 as planned, with police monitoring the area.

title: The best waterfront hotel in America is in Massachusetts, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Chatham Bars Inn in Cape Cod named the best waterfront hotel in the U.S. by USA Today readers for 2026.
Chatham Bars Inn, a historic New England destination, features a private beach and various on-site amenities.
Madison Beach Hotel in Connecticut ranked fourth in USA Today's 10Best Readers’ Choice Awards for waterfront hotels.

title: Are millionaires really leaving Massachusetts? We don’t know yet.
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: The IRS data needed to track migration of millionaires post-2023 tax is not yet available.
Massachusetts lost over 30,000 residents to other states by July 2025; income levels of movers are unknown.
The millionaires tax generated $3.4 billion in fiscal 2025, but its impact on millionaire migration remains unclear.
